A legendary yakuza once called the Dragon of Dojima, and the former Tojo Clan fourth chairman. After washing his hands of the yakuza life, he ran Morning Glory Orphanage in Okinawa with Haruka, daughter of his childhood love Yumi. He now works as a taxi driver in Nagasugai, Fukuoka under the alias Taichi Suzuki.

A legendary yakuza once called the Dragon of Dojima, and the former Tojo Clan fourth chairman. After washing his hands of the yakuza life, he ran Morning Glory Orphanage in Okinawa with Haruka, daughter of his childhood love Yumi. While working as a taxi driver in Nagasugai, Fukuoka under the alias Taichi Suzuki, he became embroiled in the events surrounding Daigo's disappearance. Asked by Madarame to protect Fukuoka's future, he took on the Tojo Clan for the Yamagasa Family and won. He then set off for Tokyo alone after Morinaga told him he'd find answers there.

Daughter of the late Yumi Sawamura, Kiryu's childhood love. After the ten billion yen heist, she moved to Okinawa with Kiryu and lived at the Morning Glory Orphanage. She has since left for Osaka, where she is training night and day to make her debut as an idol.

Owner of Nagasu Taxi. Despite the pressures of running a new taxi company in a place like Nagasugai, where competition between rival cab firms is fierce, he always seems to maintain his smile. A 30-year veteran of the industry, his employees have a lot of trust in him. Like many men from Kyushu, he's laid-back and loves to drink. Six months ago, he found Kiryu wandering Hakata and took him under his wing.

Owner of Nagasu Taxi. Despite the pressures of running a new taxi company in a place like Nagasugai, where competition between rival cab firms is fierce, he always seems to maintain his smile. A 30-year veteran of the industry, his employees have a lot of trust in him. Like many men from Kyushu, he's laid-back and loves to drink. Six months ago, he found Kiryu wandering Hakata and took him under his wing. After Kiryu spoke of his past as he prepared to take on the Tojo Clan, Nakajima told him to come back someday and rejected his resignation.

The top hostess at Olivier, a club in Nagasugai. She came to like Kiryu after he saved her from some local yakuza. Since then, she's spent a lot of time at Kiryu's apartment, looking after him whether he wants her to or not. They still aren't officially a couple, and she seems frustrated at Kiryu's lack of interest in taking the relationship further.

The top hostess at Olivier, a club in Nagasugai. She came to like Kiryu after he saved her from some local yakuza. Since then, she's spent a lot of time at Kiryu's apartment, looking after him whether he wants her to or not. She is also the daughter of Yamagasa Family patriarch, Madarame. She feels guilty for deceiving Kiryu, as her feelings for him were real. Still, she couldn't share this with him, as she knew that he'd one day leave her.

Current chairman of the Tojo Clan, which at 30,000 members is the largest yakuza group in Kanto. After the conflict with the Ueno Seiwa Clan, he shored up his financial base in Kamurocho Hills and recruited new blood. However, with war threatening to break out between East and West due to the Omi Alliance seventh chairman falling ill, he came up with a plan to bring local families from Hakata, Sapporo, and Nagoya under the Tojo banner. He has come to Nagasugai as part of these negotiations.

Current chairman of the Tojo Clan, which at 30,000 members is the largest yakuza group in Kanto. With the truce between East and West threatening to break due to the Omi Alliance seventh chairman falling ill, he came up with a plan to bring local families from Hakata, Sapporo, and Nagoya under the Tojo banner. While in Nagasugai for these negotiations, he got wind of Aoyama's betrayal and has gone into hiding to investigate the conspiracy behind it.

Current chief of Tojo Clan headquarters and assistant to Daigo Dojima. A shrewd man who runs a tight ship within the Tojo Clan in an attempt to eliminate any weaknesses. He has promoted newer families who pledge loyalty and produce results, while mercilessly cutting off senior families who cause scandals, and this austerity has earned him no shortage of criticism. Although he doesn't bring as much muscle to the table as the Majima Family, there's no doubt he's the real second-in-command within the Tojo Clan now.

Once chief of Tojo Clan headquarters, and assistant to Daigo Dojima. A shrewd man who ran a tight ship within the Tojo Clan in an attempt to eliminate any weaknesses. He planned to kill Daigo during negotiations with the Yamagasa Family, but Daigo caught on and went underground. After taking the helm due to the chairman's disappearance, he turned on Madarame. He then challenged Yahata and took on the Yamagasa Family, but was foiled by Kiryu. Just as he was about to reveal who masterminded the plot, he was shot dead by Morinaga.

Bodyguard to Tojo Clan Chairman Daigo Dojima. Always cordial and eager to follow orders to the letter, he carries out his duties together with Aizawa. He was held responsible for Daigo's disappearance after the talks with Madarame in Nagasugai and is frantically searching the area for him with Aizawa.

Bodyguard to Tojo Clan Chairman Daigo Dojima. Always cordial and eager to follow orders to the letter, he carries out his duties together with Aizawa. He was held responsible for Daigo's disappearance after the talks with Madarame in Nagasugai, and frantically searched the area for him with Aizawa before he was shot by Aoyama. He later appeared at the battle between the Tojo Clan and Yamagasa Family, where he killed Aoyama and told Kiryu to go to Tokyo.

Bodyguard to Tojo Clan Chairman Daigo Dojima. Normally a silent shade at Morinaga's side, once he's riled up, it's hard to calm him down. He was put in a tight spot after Daigo disappeared following the talks with Madarame in Nagasugai, and now he and Morinaga are searching frantically for him.

Bodyguard to Tojo Clan Chairman Daigo Dojima. Normally a silent shade at Morinaga's side, once he's riled up, it's hard to calm him down. He was put in a tight spot after Daigo disappeared following the talks with Madarame in Nagasugai, and he and Morinaga searched frantically for him. He went to see Morinaga in the hospital after his mentor was shot by Aoyama, but Morinaga killed him to cover up the plot.

Known as the most militant member of the Omi Alliance now that Ryuji Goda, the Dragon of Kansai, is gone. He wears his heart on his sleeve and loves a good fight. He considers himself the natural choice for the eighth Omi chairman, but instead of vying for support from his peers, he focuses on his archrivals, the Tojo Clan. He laments the weakened state of the Tojo Clan and visits Kiryu to persuade him to rejoin, in order to provide a worthy opponent. Though he has sworn brotherhood with the Tojo Clan's Aoyama, this was a strategic move ordered by the seventh Omi chairman and not one born of personal ties.

Known as the most militant member of the Omi Alliance now that Ryuji Goda, the Dragon of Kansai, is gone. He wears his heart on his sleeve and loves a good fight. He considers himself the natural choice for the eighth Omi chairman, and instead of vying for support from his peers, he focuses on his archrivals, the Tojo Clan. He laments the weakened state of the Tojo Clan and visits Kiryu to persuade him to rejoin in order to provide a worthy opponent. He saw Kiryu's power for himself during the battle between the Tojo Clan and the Yamagasa Family. Afterward, he returned to Osaka to prepare for war.

Patriarch of the Yamagasa Family, a yakuza group that controls the Nagasugai entertainment district in Fukuoka. He knows the strength of the Yamagasa Family pales in comparison to that of the Tojo Clan and Omi Alliance, so he seeks peace rather than conflict. Being an old-school yakuza, he values etiquette and treats even the much younger Daigo Dojima with the respect of an equal.

Patriarch of the Yamagasa Family, a yakuza group that controls the Nagasugai entertainment district in Fukuoka. He knows the strength of the Yamagasa Family pales in comparison to that of the Tojo Clan and Omi Alliance, so he seeks peace rather than conflict. Being an old-school yakuza, he values etiquette and treats even the much younger Daigo Dojima with the respect of an equal. He was badly injured when Aoyama turned on him during negotiations with the Tojo Clan. He moves to dissolve the Yamagasa Family to avoid a full-scale war, but Kiryu rejects this in front of Yahata.

A typical hot-blooded Kyushu man who tends to let his fists do the talking. Fiercely loyal, he wouldn't hesitate to lay his life on the line for his boss, Madarame. He trades blows with Kiryu after Aoyama paints him as Madarame's attacker. He's prepared to go to war to get revenge on the Tojo Clan.

A typical hot-blooded Kyushu man who tends to let his fists do the talking. Fiercely loyal, he wouldn't hesitate to lay his life on the line for his boss Madarame. He trades blows with Kiryu after Aoyama paints him as Madarame's attacker. He was gunning for war in order to get revenge on the Tojo Clan, but Kiryu convinced him to leave the fate of the Yamagasa Family in his hands. He watched as Kiryu took down the Tojo Clan all alone, true to his word.

A detective with the organized crime unit of the Osaka Prefectural Police. He is trying to stop the impending war between the Omi and the Tojo without involving the Tokyo Metropolitan Police. He came to Fukuoka following Watase of the Omi Alliance. After Daigo's disappearance, he questioned Kiryu, who was the last to see him. He then asked Kiryu to calm the unrest, as the police had their hands tied.

A detective with the organized crime unit of the Osaka Prefectural Police. He is trying to stop the impending war between the Omi and the Tojo without involving the Tokyo Metropolitan Police. He came to Fukuoka following Watase of the Omi Alliance. After Daigo's disappearance, he questioned Kiryu, who was the last to see him. He then asked Kiryu to calm the unrest, as the police had their hands tied. He convinced a reluctant Kiryu to go to Tokyo after he settled things between the Yamagasa Family and Tojo Clan, bringing up Majima's death.

A legendary yakuza who spent 25 years behind bars after being convicted of killing eighteen members of a rival organization. After the events of 2010, he rejoined the Tojo Clan as patriarch of his own family. He and Majima are sworn brothers who pledged to hold the Tojo Clan together.

A legendary yakuza who spent 25 years behind bars after being convicted of killing eighteen members of a rival organization. After the events of 2010, he rejoined the Tojo Clan as patriarch of his own family. He and Majima are sworn brothers who pledged to hold the Tojo Clan together. He has accepted the position of Tojo Clan captain but chose to go to prison to pay for his crimes first.

A legendary yakuza who spent 25 years behind bars after being convicted of killing eighteen members of a rival organization. After the events of 2010, he rejoined the Tojo Clan as patriarch of his own family. He and Majima are sworn brothers who pledged to hold the Tojo Clan together. He accepted the position of Tojo Clan captain, but chose to go to prison to pay for his crimes first. Upon hearing of Majima's death, he broke out and went to Tsukimino to find answers. After Baba's betrayal, he learned that there was a mastermind behind the plot and struck a deal with an Osakan detective to go to Tokyo.

A militant yakuza once feared as the Mad Dog of Shimano. He strove to rebuild the clan after quitting his lieutenant post to assume an advisory role a few years ago, but was unhappy with the new generation's focus on making money rather than fighting. After Saejima's return, he was reminded of the need for strong, old-school yakuza, and together they pledged to support Daigo.
